chronology.event: Inaba reacts to Shiki remark: claims first six months after surgery remained confined indoors, then transferred to another clinic with yard, later released with money and medicine conditional on controls. Once he attempted to deviate from assigned route, was refused weekly drugs at another medical stop. Patient claims supervisors somehow knew where he traveled; unknown if actual surveillance. Seina records as patient's testimony, not proven.

Optical/metallurgical examination of plate M-4 / 031 (5x3cm, ~2mm): nickel-copper-rich alloy under protective finish, regular machine-engraved lettering, serial production likely. Four wave-like strokes resembling but NOT matching official Kiri motif engraved later with different tool. Six standardized edge notches, four filled dark polymer with different application characteristics at fourth. Their meaning undetermined.

Precautionary chakra micro-sensing reveals fine deliberately conductive inset paths under plate protective layer forming central contour around M-4/031, six peripheral cells and high-residual-conductance contact around tether hole. Looks like passive fuinjutsu tag/readable ID, no observable active chakra source or remote transmission under low passive scan. Unknown stronger activation and exact format. Inaba volunteers clue: physicians placed plate into plate-size ring recessed reader which unlocked medication drawer. This is patient's anecdote consistent with passive access key.

Raking light and depth analysis reveals earlier partially erased under-surface engraving: 'R-031 / 4', 'T.C. — [unreadable]', 'Серия: 17'. Potential but unproven overlap of '17' with old Kusa 'К-17' consultant record; no letter K on plate, DO NOT treat as same network automatically. R could mean recipient but unproved. Seina questions what '4' labels.

Micro-sample from exposed fourth notch analyzed: dark polymer carries organic constituent with protein-binding potential; too little to identify as immunosuppressant, biological marker or reader reagent. Seina stores in sealed vial and plans compare with genuine drug residue if obtained. Patient claims last physician said next monitoring would be 'заключительным', and 'После следующего контроля решим, нужен ли ты нам дальше', making him visibly afraid.

Seina notes no transmitter detected, tag may identify holder when presented to matched reader. Original plate intact, fourth-notch microsample sealed. She asks Shiki conceptually who controls readers. Patient asks if operators can locate him; Seina only says no active transmitter observed, not proof of absence of outside surveillance. Tissue histology and cell compatibility results still pending.
